findings.title: GHSA-3cfg-jpcr-gfp3: Version catalog values run as code in generated accessors
findings.summary_md: Gradle writes version catalog values into generated Java accessor source without escaping them, so a crafted version, dependency coordinate or plugin id adds code that runs with the privileges of the build user when Gradle loads the catalog during settings evaluation. The code runs in every build that imports or defines the catalog, including IDE synchronization and builds that use no catalog entry. Affected org.gradle:gradle-core ranges are 7.0 through 8.14.6 and 9.0.0 through 9.9.0; the fix versions are 9.9.1 and 8.14.7 in the open source distribution, with 9.8.3, 9.7.3, 9.6.3, 9.5.3, 9.4.3, 9.3.3, 9.2.3 and 7.6.8 under the Gradle Security Subscription. Rated critical at CVSS 4.0 9.3; no CVE id is assigned in the advisory. Gradle states a proof of concept exists and is not published.

findings.title: Gradle 9.9.1 release: three security fixes in the 9.x line
findings.summary_md: Gradle 9.9.1 is the first patch release for 9.9.0 and the release notes list the three security vulnerabilities it addresses: version catalog values run as code in generated accessors (9.3 critical), Gradle client trusts the content of the daemon registry (8.6 high), and daemon client trusts stale registry entries through port squatting (7.0 high). The release also carries Kotlin DSL incremental compilation and Problems API grouping changes unrelated to security.

findings.title: Gradle 8.14.7 release: security patch for the 8.x line
findings.summary_md: Gradle 8.14.7 is the seventh patch release for Gradle 8.14 and addresses the same three security vulnerabilities fixed in 9.9.1, with the version catalog code injection rated 9.3 critical. It is the open source fix for all 8.x builds still on 8.14.6 or earlier.

findings.title: GHSA-gqrr-4j89-5267: Gradle client trusts the content of the daemon registry
findings.summary_md: The org.gradle.daemon.registry.base property is honoured from a project's gradle.properties, so a project can point the client at a registry file it ships. The client deserializes parts of that file with Java serialization and connects to any address it lists, including a remote host, although daemons only listen locally. Rated high at CVSS 4.0 8.6 and fixed in 9.9.1 and 8.14.7.

findings.title: GHSA-pcp8-98xm-c6pr: Daemon client trusts stale registry entries (port squatting)
findings.summary_md: When a daemon dies without cleaning up its registry entry, its loopback port is free while the registry still points at it, so a local user who binds that port receives the next build request from the victim's client. The daemon is not authenticated to the client and the client does not check that the recorded daemon process is still running. Rated high at CVSS 4.0 7.0 and fixed in 9.9.1 and 8.14.7.
